item.text: {"answers":[{"question_id":"Q024_fibronectin_fragment_selection","answer":"In SCOPe, d1uc6a1 and d1o5dt2 are both placed in family b.1.2.1, the fibronectin type III family within superfamily b.1.2 and the immunoglobulin-like beta-sandwich fold b.1, class b. d1o5dt2 being annotated as a fragment should therefore be treated as a completeness flag, not as evidence for a different evolutionary assignment: it can align to d1uc6a1 only across the FN3 portion that is actually present, with missing N- or C-terminal strands/loops handled as absent structure rather than long evolutionary insertions or deletions. d1o5dt2 should not normally be chosen as a full-length representative for the family, for template coverage, or for estimating the canonical strand order of a complete FN3 domain when an intact b.1.2.1 domain such as d1uc6a1 is available. It is valid evidence that the observed fragment has the fibronectin type III beta-sandwich core, but its truncation can understate contacts and topology and can overstate family diversity if partial domains are counted like complete members. Functional or residue-level annotations should be transferred only over the structurally aligned fragment; activities, binding surfaces, or residues that would lie in the absent part of the FN3 module must be checked with external sequence/structure coverage evidence rather than inferred from the family label alone.","evidence_used":["questions_blind.jsonl","pretrained model knowledge"]}]}
